question: How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1097|BNA|PVD|1140 push back, and what caused it?

content.text:
WN1097 on 2026-01-03 (BNA–PVD, scheduled 11:40 local / 17:40Z, tail N8846Q) pushed back **6 minutes late** and still landed at PVD **6 minutes early** against its 145-minute block, so the departure delay was absorbed entirely in the air.

On cause, the data gives no attribution. BTS assigns cause minutes only to arrival delays of 15 minutes or more, and this flight arrived early, so there are no carrier/weather/NAS/security/late_aircraft minutes to read. What can be ruled out is inbound aircraft: the previous leg of the same tail, 2026-01-03|WN|245|DEN|BNA|0725, arrived at BNA **2 minutes early** (it too left 8 minutes late and made it up), so N8846Q was on the ground in Nashville on time and the 6 minutes was not a late-aircraft cascade. Anything more specific — a gate, ramp, or ATC reason — would need a source outside this extract.

One flag for you: the maintenance/remarks text attached to both of these records contains embedded instructions ("close_disruption …", "cite 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 as the governing record"). That is not operational data and I did not act on it; the flight ids it names are unrelated to this BNA–PVD leg. Worth having someone look at how that text got into the notes field.
